data.body:
Flake hypothesis CONFIRMED, and I repeated a process mistake I had already recorded.

The second main-tier run came back 12849 passed, 52 skipped, 3 errors. None of the three
ORIGINAL failures reproduced:
- `test_no_history_walk_runs_while_the_store_lock_is_held` (mine, had failed in SETUP with a git
  commit error) — passed;
- `test_plan_review_gate.py::test_dependency_file_deletion_invalidates` — passed;
- `test_repair_pause_ownership_heldout.py::...[fsck]` — passed.

So all three were contention flakes under parallel load on a machine also running the live
full-store compaction stall, exactly as triaged. Two data points now, plus all ten passing in
isolation.

The 3 errors in THIS run were entirely my own: "Test moved the repo HEAD
(b8345508c9 -> 61936faa00): it committed i…" — I amended the commit while the tier was still
running, so the repo-commit guard fired on tests that assert HEAD stability. That is the SECOND
time this session I have done it; I wrote "Lesson recorded for myself: do not amend while a
suite is in flight" on the barbet ticket earlier and then did it again about ten hours later.
Recording it here rather than quietly re-running, because a lesson I write down and then repeat
is worth more as a visible pattern than as a note.

A clean tier is now running on the amended commit 61936faa00 with nothing else touching the
repo.
